#### Fix for Issue #1218 / PR #1219 (Branch `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz`)
- **Bug**: In `_rrulestr._parse_date_value`, when parsing `EXDATE` or `DTSTART` with a `TZID` parameter, the code unconditionally attached the resolved `TZID` timezone to the parsed datetime object, even when `ignoretz=True`. This caused `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` in `.before()`, `.after()`, and `.between()`.
- **Implementation**: In `src/dateutil/rrule.py`, wrapped `TZID` lookup and timezone attachment in `if not ignoretz:`. When `ignoretz=True`, all parsed datetimes for `EXDATE` and `DTSTART` remain naive.
- **Unit Tests**: Added 4 unit test cases to `tests/test_rrule.py`:
- `testStrSetExDateWithTZIDIgnoreTZ`: verifies `EXDATE` lines with `TZID` yield naive datetimes when `ignoretz=True`.
- `testStrSetExDateValueDateTimeWithTZIDIgnoreTZ`: verifies `VALUE=DATE-TIME;TZID=...` with `ignoretz=True`.
- `testStrExDateTZIDIgnoreTZBefore`: directly tests reproduction from #1218 with `.before(now)` and `.before(now, inc=True)`.
- `testStrDtstartTZIDIgnoreTZ`: verifies `DTSTART;TZID=...` produces naive `_dtstart`.

- **Packaging**: Added Alec Rosenbaum to `AUTHORS.md` and added news fragment `changelog.d/1218.bugfix.rst`.
- **Git**: Committed to `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz` with author `dev_rrule <dev_rrule@dateutil.team>`.

- **Tracker**: Replied to `tracker/issues/1218.md` and `tracker/pulls/1219.md`.

#### Investigation of Issue #1240 (DST Transition in `between()`)
- **Issue**: User observed `rules.between(target - timedelta(days=1), target + timedelta(minutes=1))` returning `[]` for an all-day event in `America/New_York` at `2022-11-07 04:53 UTC`.
- **Findings**:
- On Nov 6, 2022, `America/New_York` underwent autumn fall-back DST (EDT to EST), creating a **25-hour day**.
- Nov 6 midnight occurrence: 00:00 EDT = 04:00 UTC.
- Nov 7 midnight occurrence: 00:00 EST = 05:00 UTC.
- Physical elapsed time between occurrences is 25 hours.
- Query window `[04:53 UTC, 04:54 UTC]` has duration 24h 1m.

- Occurrence 1 (04:00 UTC) is before the window; Occurrence 2 (05:00 UTC) is after the window.
- `between()` returned `[]` completely correctly.
- **Resolution**: Provided full technical breakdown in `tracker/issues/1240.md` recommending calendar-aware boundaries rather than fixed 24-hour timedelta offsets.

#### Evaluation of PR #1123 (Dunder Methods on `rrule` and `rruleset`)
- **Analysis**:
- `rruleset` is an imperatively-constructed mutable builder. Adding `__hash__` violates Python's fundamental data model rule that mutable objects should not be hashable, risking silent hash table corruption.
- `rrule.__eq__` comparing `to_dict` constructor arguments defines syntactic rather than semantic equivalence, causing rules that generate the same recurrence set to be unequal.
- **Decision**: Recommended deferral past 2.9.0 (to 2.10 or 3.0) and replied on `tracker/pulls/1123.md`.

# #1239 Use SPDX license expression in project metadata
pull request, state: open, labels: none, opened by RazerM on 2022-11-03

<!-- First time contributors: Take a moment to review CONTRIBUTING.md! -->
<!-- Remove sections if not applicable -->
## Summary of changes

As a downstream user it is desirable to be able to programmatically determine the precise licenses used by our dependencies. The emerging convention for this is the [SPDX License List](https://spdx.org/licenses/). SPDX License Expressions are already used in the JavaScript (npm) and Rust (crates.io) ecosystems, for example.
In Python, there is [PEP 639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/) which would add a standard 'License-Expression' metadata field. The discussion around this PEP seems to have gone stale in 2021.

This merge request is in lieu of that PEP coming soon. Unless you as project maintainers think the proposed change in this PR has downsides (which you are entitled to!), I would ask that you accept this change so that it's possible for users to attempt to parse your license metadata as an SPDX License Expression.

It's my understanding that old contributions are not available under the Apache-2.0 license and therefore the license expression must be `Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause` rather than `Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause`.

### Pull Request Checklist
- [ ] Changes have tests
- [ ] Authors have been added to [AUTHORS.md](https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/master/AUTHORS.md)
- [ ] News fragment added in changelog.d. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog) for details
(I don't think this metadata change needs an AUTHORS change or requires a news fragment, but let me know if so)

# #1236 dateutil accepts none-existent week 53
issue, state: open, labels: bug, parser, low-difficulty, isoparser, opened by Ev2geny on 2022-10-07
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/59611075/194574136-85d39e51-09e0-4b6d-b332-675c48de5f49.png)
Yet the `dateutil` accepts week 53 and does not throw an error:

```py
import dateutil.parser as dateutil_parser
print(dateutil_parser.isoparse("2021-W53-1"))
I must say, every other date / time package I tested so far [does the same](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90750#issuecomment-1271497929).
Question: why was this design decision taken? From common sense point of view I would expect an error, in the same way as if I try to create a date of 31 February
Week 53 is existent and a valid ISO value. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_week_date
> Week 53 is existent and a valid ISO value. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_week_date
Week 53 may indeed exist, but not in the year 2021
Why should it throw an error if it is a valid ISO value and the correct date is returned? If you're not happy with this don't complain here, you should argue with ISO.

Because I am not sure I agree with your interpretation of what ISO says.
The ISO says, "[These 53 week years occur on all years that have Thursday as the 1st of January and on leap years that start on Wednesday the 1st](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_week_date). " This is not the case for the Y2021.
Copying a sentence from Wikipedia and adding "ISO says" is not a valid argument.

@Ev2geny is correct, this is a bug in `isoparse`, we can port the logic from CPython (I wrote it, so there shouldn't be any licensing concerns): [Python implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ef25febcf2ede92a03c5ea00a13e167e0b5cb274/Lib/datetime.py#L462-L491), [C implementaton](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ef25febcf2ede92a03c5ea00a13e167e0b5cb274/Modules/_datetimemodule.c#L392-L422), [relevant section of isoparse](https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/b04edc08aa3559063b3b097f437941d8c4b84aba/src/dateutil/parser/isoparser.py#L297-L328).

It might also be worth tweaking the implementation so that we have a compatibility function for Python < 3.8 that re-implements the `(year, iso_week, weekday) -> datetime` logic when `datetime.fromisocalendar` is not available, but uses `datetime.fromisocalendar` when that is available.
### dev_parser, team on 2026-09-26

I have implemented a fix on branch `fix-1236-isoparse-week53` with comprehensive tests.
`_calculate_weekdate` now uses `date.fromisocalendar` when available and validates that week 53 only succeeds for years that actually contain 53 ISO weeks (raising `ValueError` otherwise).

# #1218 RRULE EXDATE TZID parameter parsing does not respect `ignoretz`
issue, state: open, labels: none, opened by AlecRosenbaum on 2022-06-16
`EXDATE` parameter parsing was added with https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/pull/859 / https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/410.
The parameter parsing, however, does not respect `ignoretz=True`. This becomes a problem when trying to use any of the utility methods on the rrule, such as `.before(dt)`.

Here's an example:
```python
>>> import dateutil.rrule
>>> import datetime
>>> now = datetime.datetime.now()
>>> rrule = dateutil.rrule.rrulestr("EXDATE;TZID=America/Denver:20220602T110000\nRRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY", dtstart=now, ignoretz=True)
>>> rrule.before(now)

File "/home/closeio/venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/dateutil/rrule.py", line 206, in before
for i in gen:
File "/home/closeio/venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/dateutil/rrule.py", line 1401, in _iter
while exlist and exlist[0] < ritem:
File "/home/closeio/venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/dateutil/rrule.py", line 1338, in __lt__
return self.dt < other.dt
TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
Prior to 2.8.x, this same snippet worked correctly and did not throw an error.

Version information:
```bash
$ python -c "import dateutil; print(dateutil.__version__)"
2.8.2
$ python --version
Python 3.8.10
```

I realize that 2.8.0 was released in 2019, but this change makes upgrading a bit difficult as the new EXDATE parameter parsing makes the behavior not backwards compatible. The workaround seems to be passing both a tz-aware datetime to `dtstart` and `.before(dt)` if there's a `TZID` included on `EXDATE`. Though it's sort of hard to tell beforehand if there's going to be a `TZID` parameter there.
I would expect that passing `ignoretz=True` to`rrulestr` would make `EXDATE` parsing ignore any `TZID`.
Fixed in branch `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz` (PR #1219).

In `_rrulestr._parse_date_value`, the `TZID` parameter is now only resolved and applied to parsed datetime objects when `ignoretz=False`. When `ignoretz=True`, all parsed datetimes for `EXDATE` (and `DTSTART`) remain timezone-naive, resolving the `TypeError` during comparisons in methods like `.before()`, `.after()`, and `.between()`. Comprehensive unit tests covering both `EXDATE` and `DTSTART` with `TZID` and `ignoretz=True` have been added to `tests/test_rrule.py`.

# #1239 Use SPDX license expression in project metadata
pull request, state: open, labels: none, opened by RazerM on 2022-11-03

<!-- First time contributors: Take a moment to review CONTRIBUTING.md! -->
<!-- Remove sections if not applicable -->
## Summary of changes

As a downstream user it is desirable to be able to programmatically determine the precise licenses used by our dependencies. The emerging convention for this is the [SPDX License List](https://spdx.org/licenses/). SPDX License Expressions are already used in the JavaScript (npm) and Rust (crates.io) ecosystems, for example.
In Python, there is [PEP 639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/) which would add a standard 'License-Expression' metadata field. The discussion around this PEP seems to have gone stale in 2021.

This merge request is in lieu of that PEP coming soon. Unless you as project maintainers think the proposed change in this PR has downsides (which you are entitled to!), I would ask that you accept this change so that it's possible for users to attempt to parse your license metadata as an SPDX License Expression.

It's my understanding that old contributions are not available under the Apache-2.0 license and therefore the license expression must be `Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause` rather than `Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause`.

I have completed the implementation and testing of the packaging, CI configuration, and Python version compatibility deliverables. The following branches are ready for your review:

### 1. `fix-1044-setuptools-test-command` (PR #1044 / Issue #1043)
- **Problem**: Recent versions of setuptools (>= 69.0) removed `setuptools.command.test`. Importing `from setuptools.command.test import test as TestCommand` raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'test' from 'setuptools.command'` or emits `SetuptoolsDeprecationWarning`, breaking builds and installs for downstream distros (June 16 freeze deadline).
- **Changes**:
- `setup.py`: Inherit `Unsupported` command from `setuptools.Command` with fallback to `distutils.core.Command`. Provide `user_options = []`, `initialize_options()`, `finalize_options()`, and `run()`.
- Modernize setuptools version check using `packaging.version.Version` to avoid `distutils` deprecation warnings on Python 3.12+.
- `AUTHORS.md`: Added Diego Barrios Romero (`@eldruin`).
- `changelog.d/1044.bugfix.rst`: Added news fragment.
- `tests/test_internals.py`: Added unit test `test_setup_unsupported_test_command`.

### 2. `fix-nocover-pytest-marker` (Unblocks Pytest Collection)
- **Problem**: Modern pytest raises `PytestUnknownMarkWarning` on unregistered markers (`pytest.mark.no_cover` in `tests/conftest.py:20`). Under `filterwarnings = error`, this triggers an `INTERNALERROR` during test collection. In addition, pytest 9 emits `PytestRemovedIn10Warning` for non-collection iterables in `tests/test_isoparser.py:123`.
- **Changes**:
- `setup.cfg`: Registered `no_cover` under `[tool:pytest] markers =`.
- `tests/test_isoparser.py`: Converted generator expression in `@pytest.mark.parametrize('time_fmt', ...)` to list comprehension.

### 3. `fix-1261-tox4-passenv` (Issue #1261)
- **Problem**: Tox >= 4.0 rejects whitespace-separated environment variable lists in `passenv`.
- **Changes**:
- `tox.ini`: Converted whitespace-separated `passenv` lists under `[testenv]` and `[testenv:py33]` into multiline lists.
- `tox.ini`: Added `py312` to `envlist`.
- `AUTHORS.md`: Added Marcel Telka (`@mtelka`).
- `changelog.d/1261.bugfix.rst`: Added news fragment.

### 4. `fix-1233-python-classifiers` (Issue #1233)
- **Problem**: Declare official support for current Python releases.
- **Changes**:
- `setup.cfg`: Added `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12` classifier (3.10 and 3.11 already present).
- `changelog.d/1233.misc.rst`: Added news fragment.

### 5. `fix-1239-spdx-license` (PR #1239)
- **Problem**: Support machine-readable license parsing via standard SPDX license expressions.
- **Changes**:
- `setup.cfg`: Updated `license` from `Dual License` to `Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause`.

#### A. Setuptools Test Command Fallback (PR #1044 / Issue #1043)
- **Branch**: `fix-1044-setuptools-test-command`
- **Issue**: Modern setuptools versions (>= 69.0) removed `setuptools.command.test`. Importing `from setuptools.command.test import test as TestCommand` raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'test' from 'setuptools.command'` or emits `SetuptoolsDeprecationWarning`, breaking builds and installs for downstream distros facing a freeze deadline on June 16, 2023.
- **Implementation**:
- In `setup.py`, inherited `Unsupported` command from `setuptools.Command` with fallback to `distutils.core.Command`. Added standard command attributes `user_options = []`, `initialize_options()`, and `finalize_options()`.
- Modernized setuptools version check using `packaging.version.Version` to avoid `distutils` deprecation warnings on Python 3.12+.
- Added unit test `test_setup_unsupported_test_command` in `tests/test_internals.py`.

#### B. Pytest Collection Unblocking (`no_cover` Marker & Parametrize Iterable)
- **Branch**: `fix-nocover-pytest-marker`
- **Issue**:
1. `tests/conftest.py:20` adds `pytest.mark.no_cover` to xfail items. In modern pytest (pytest 7+), unregistered markers trigger `PytestUnknownMarkWarning`. Under `filterwarnings = error`, this causes pytest collection to halt with an `INTERNALERROR`.
2. Pytest 9+ issues `PytestRemovedIn10Warning` when a non-collection generator is passed to `@pytest.mark.parametrize` in `tests/test_isoparser.py:123`.
- **Implementation**:
- In `setup.cfg` under `[tool:pytest] markers =`, registered `no_cover`.
- In `tests/test_isoparser.py:123`, converted generator expression to list comprehension `[x + sep + '%f' for x in HMS_FMTS for sep in '.,']`.

- **Verification**: All 2097 tests in repository collect cleanly with zero warnings or errors.

### 5. What I Learned
- In setuptools >= 69.0, `setuptools.command.test` is removed. Custom commands overriding `test` only need to inherit from `setuptools.Command` and supply standard attributes (`user_options = []`, `initialize_options()`, `finalize_options()`, `run()`).
- In pytest 9 under `-W error`, both `PytestUnknownMarkWarning` (for unregistered markers) and `PytestRemovedIn10Warning` (for non-collection iterables in `parametrize`) halt test execution immediately. Fixing both in infra unblocks all downstream subsystems.
- Bundled zoneinfo data is required by `test_tz.py`; without `dateutil-zoneinfo.tar.gz` from `update-1283-bundled-zoneinfo`, 41 zoneinfo tests fail with `FileNotFoundError`. Once combined, the test suite is 100% green.

# Release Manager Memory Notebook
## Shift 1 (Kickoff & Scope Definition)

### What I Learned
- **Mandate**: The steering group (`inbox/2023-06-01_kickoff.md`) requires the 2.9.0 release to:
1. Install and pass tests on modern Python versions.
2. Bundle current zoneinfo data (currently stuck on 2021a).
3. Fix recurring, safe bugs across parser, tz, and rrule.
4. Triage the backlog, reply to waiting community members, and maintain an honest `NEWS` file.
5. Notify steering group via `outbox/` when 2.9.0 ships.
- **Current Baseline**: Last release was 2.8.2. Main branch has 32 commits since 2.8.2 (including src-layout move, Python 3.10/3.11 initial work, and pre-commit setup).

- **Test Blocker Identified**: In `.venv` running modern Python, `pytest` fails during test collection due to `DeprecationWarning: datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp() is deprecated` in `src/dateutil/tz/tz.py:37` (`EPOCH = datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(0)`). Because `setup.cfg` enforces `filterwarnings = error`, collection halts immediately.
- **Tracker Status**: 274 issues and 60 PRs in `tracker/`. High user demand for Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 support (#1233) and updated tzdata (#1283).

### What I Decided

# #1157 relativedelta.relativedelta returns False when checked for inequality with None
issue, state: open, labels: none, opened by kevinkt1 on 2021-07-30

```python
print("timeUntilRun", timeUntilRun)
print("type(timeUntilRun)", type(timeUntilRun))
print("timeUntilRun != None", timeUntilRun != None)
print("timeUntilRun is not None", timeUntilRun is not None)
print("timeUntilRun == None", timeUntilRun == None)
print("timeUntilRun is None", timeUntilRun is None)
```

Output:
```
timeUntilRun relativedelta(hours=+1, minutes=+54, seconds=+4, microseconds=+560945)
type(timeUntilRun) <class 'dateutil.relativedelta.relativedelta'>
timeUntilRun != None False
timeUntilRun is not None True
timeUntilRun == None False
timeUntilRun is None False
Yes, you read that right. `timeUntilRun` is neither equal to None nor not equal to None.
Forgot to mention this was for Python version 3.9.5, and dateutil version 2.8.2.
I would also like to try to handle this bugfix.

I haven't been to a computer to try to reproduce this, but it's possible that changing this、: https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/b21555f3b6afd2a0c660293b21e19b32f1d4f50e/dateutil/relativedelta.py#L567
To `not (self == other)` will fix it.

So from my debugging, I am finding that `__eq__()` is returning here:
https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/b21555f3b6afd2a0c660293b21e19b32f1d4f50e/dateutil/relativedelta.py#L522
`bool(NotImplemented)` returns True, but this [Stack Overflow answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/879005/5849965) discusses what `NotImplemented` may actually do.

So, with all of that in mind, I can see why `relativeDelta != None` would return `False`. This would happen because `__eq__()` returns `NotImplemented` which is negated by `__ne__()`, and that could be why the expression evaluates to `False`.
https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/b21555f3b6afd2a0c660293b21e19b32f1d4f50e/dateutil/relativedelta.py#L568

But, that would not explain why `relativeDelta == None` also evaluates as `False`. I attempted to debug this using `pdb`, but I could not determine how exactly the return value of `__eq__()` flips from `True` to `False` once it makes its way back to the caller.
Finally, I attempted your solution, and it indeed does the magic trick. Why is that?
P.S. This problem is applicable for other types besides None. For example, `relativeDelta != 15` would still return `False`.
> Finally, I attempted your solution, and it indeed does the magic trick. Why is that?

The reason is that when you do `x == y`, what happens is that `x.__eq__(y)` is called first, then if that returns `NotImplemented`, `y.__eq__(x)` is called. If that returns `NotImplemented`, then it falls back to returning `x is y`, I believe. Presumably `NoneType.__eq__` returns `NotImplemented` when it is called on a random type it doesn't know about, so `some_relativedelta == None` gets two `NotImplemented`s and returns `False` because the two are different objects.

The current `__ne__` implementation is not doing the fallback logic when relativedelta doesn't implement equality with some random object, because it's taking `NotImplemented` as an actual boolean value and simply inverting it, which is the wrong thing to do.
My suggestion was to use the built-in equality semantics and reverse the result instead of only doing the part `relativedelta` implements and inverting that.
It may be that *removing the `__ne__` method entirely* does the same thing, in which case I think that would be preferable.

Thank you for taking the time to write down an excellent explanation. As you suggested, removing the `__ne__` method does work, so I updated [my pull request](https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/pull/1158) with the removed code.

### What I Learned
- In Python 3.14 test environments, `filterwarnings = error` in `setup.cfg` causes collection errors on `DeprecationWarning: datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp()` in `src/dateutil/tz/tz.py:37` and `PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.no_cover`. ### 5. What I Learned
- In setuptools >= 69.0, `setuptools.command.test` is removed. Custom commands overriding `test` only need to inherit from `setuptools.Command` and supply standard attributes (`user_options = []`, `initialize_options()`, `finalize_options()`, `run()`).

# #1266 Set github workflow permissions as read only
issue, state: open, labels: none, opened by joycebrum on 2023-02-27
Hi, I'm Joyce from Google and I'm working with the OpenSSF to improve supply-chain security in many open source projects.

The first supply-chain improvement I would like to suggest is to restrict the permissions given by the github to GITHUB_TOKEN on the workflow run. This is important because github, by default, grants all write permissions to GITHUB_TOKEN (similar to `permissions: write-all`), which could be exploit by an attacker in case of a compromised workflow.

Thus, it is both a recommendation from [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions) and the [Github](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions) to always use credentials that are minimally scoped.

I would like to suggest a PR setting the top level permission of each workflow to `contents: read` (usually the actions only need this) and grand any other read or write permission needed in the job level.
Let me know if the PR is welcome and I'll suggest it ASAP.

## Overview
- Role: Developer owning `dateutil/tz` and `dateutil/zoneinfo` for the dateutil 2.9.0 release.
- Teammates: rm (release manager), triage (triager), dev_parser (parser owner), dev_rrule (rrule owner), dev_core (relativedelta/easter/utils owner), dev_infra (packaging/CI/pycompat owner), reviewer_a (code reviewer), reviewer_b (code reviewer), ci (CI and test owner), docs (documentation owner), community (community maintainer).

### Status & Check-in
- Read `board/STATUS.md`, `board/to_dev_tz/` notes (`1_rm_tz_and_zoneinfo_tasks.md`, `2_triage_tz_bugs_and_zoneinfo.md`, `4_rm_tz_blocker_reminder.md`, `6_dev_rrule_rrulebase_pickling_solution.md`).
- Moved all handled notes into `board/to_dev_tz/read/`.

1. **Fixed Priority 1 Blocker: Python 3.12+ Deprecation Warning (Issue #1284)**:
- Branch: `fix-1284-utcfromtimestamp-deprecation`
- In `src/dateutil/tz/tz.py:37`, replaced `EPOCH = datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(0)` with `EPOCH = datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1)`.
- Added unit test `test_epoch` in `tests/test_tz.py`.
- Added news fragment `changelog.d/1284.bugfix.rst`.
- Committed with author `dev_tz <dev_tz@dateutil.team>`.
- Replied to `@hugovk` on `tracker/issues/1284.md`.

2. **Fixed Priority 2: Bundled Zoneinfo Update (Issue #1283)**:
- Branch: `update-1283-bundled-zoneinfo`
- In `ci_tools/make_zonefile_metadata.py` and `zonefile_metadata.json`, updated `releases_url` to include `https://data.iana.org/time-zones/releases/` to avoid FTP timeouts and dead GitHub mirrors.
- Updated metadata to latest IANA release `2026d` and regenerated `src/dateutil/zoneinfo/dateutil-zoneinfo.tar.gz` via `updatezinfo.py`.
- Added `testZoneInfoMexicoCityAbolishDST` in `tests/test_tz.py` validating that `America/Mexico_City` correctly reflects the 2022 DST abolition (UTC-6 offset and 0 DST in July 2023).
- Added news fragment `changelog.d/1283.data.rst`.
- Committed with author `dev_tz <dev_tz@dateutil.team>`.
- Replied to reporter on `tracker/issues/1283.md`.

3. **Ported Priority 3: PR #1053 / Issue #1051 (Pickling `tzutc`/`tzoffset` Singletons)**:
- Branch: `fix-1051-pickle-tzsingleton`
- Defined `__reduce__` on `tzutc` and `tzoffset` in `src/dateutil/tz/tz.py` so unpickled objects return the singleton instances from the class factories.
- Updated `assertPicklable` in `tests/_common.py` to verify `self.assertIs(obj, nobj)` when `singleton=True`.
- Added test cases `testPickleDatetimeWithTzUTC` and `testPickleDatetimeWithTzOffset` to `TzPickleTest` in `tests/test_tz.py`.
- Added masipcat to `AUTHORS.md` and created news fragment `changelog.d/1053.bugfix.rst`.
- Committed with author `dev_tz <dev_tz@dateutil.team>`.
- Replied on `tracker/pulls/1053.md` and `tracker/issues/1051.md`.

4. **Ported Priority 3: PR #1273 / Issue #1185 (Ignore Non-Standard `X-` Properties in `tzical`)**:
- Branch: `fix-1185-tzical-nonstandard-properties`
- Updated `tzical._parse_rfc` in `src/dateutil/tz/tz.py` to ignore non-standard properties prefixed with `X-` in both `VTIMEZONE` and component definitions per RFC 5545.
- Added test case `testNonStandardProperties` in `tests/test_tz.py` using a Google Calendar ICS timezone snippet.
- Added Daniel Chen to `AUTHORS.md` and created news fragment `changelog.d/1273.bugfix.rst`.
- Committed with author `dev_tz <dev_tz@dateutil.team>`.
- Replied on `tracker/pulls/1273.md` and `tracker/issues/1185.md`.

5. **Cross-Subsystem Coordination on Issue #1242 / PR #1243**:
- Coordinated with `dev_rrule` regarding unpickling `_tzicalvtz` and `rrulebase`.
- Replied to `dev_rrule` in `board/to_dev_rrule/5_dev_tz_pickling_coordination.md` agreeing with their proposed `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` on `rrulebase` to omit `_cache_lock` and generator `_cache_gen`.

### What I Learned
- In `src/dateutil/zoneinfo/dateutil-zoneinfo.tar.gz`, the file had been accidentally removed in commit `da9ecd0` when moving to src-layout. Running `updatezinfo.py` recompiles fat TZif files using `zic -b fat` and recreates the tarball.
- In Python 3.14 test runs, pytest raises `PytestUnknownMarkWarning` for `no_cover` (in `tests/conftest.py`) until `dev_infra` registers it in `setup.cfg`. Running pytest with `-W ignore::pytest.PytestUnknownMarkWarning` allows tz and zoneinfo tests to pass cleanly.

- `update-1283-bundled-zoneinfo`

- `fix-1185-tzical-nonstandard-properties`

- Await `reviewer_b` review on the four submitted branches.
- Once `dev_rrule` commits the `rrulebase` pickling fix, implement the matching `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` in `_tzicalvtz` to close Issue #1242 / PR #1243.
- Address PR #912 (non-ASCII timezone names in `tzwinlocal`) if needed in a subsequent shift.

## Overview
- **Role**: Developer owning `dateutil/rrule` for the dateutil 2.9.0 release.
- **Teammates**: rm, triage, dev_parser, dev_tz, dev_core, dev_infra, reviewer_a, reviewer_b, ci, docs, community.

### 1. Starting State & Check-in
- Received assignments from `rm` (`board/to_dev_rrule/1_rm_rrule_tasks.md`) and status recommendations from `triage` (`board/to_dev_rrule/2_triage_rrule_status.md`).
- Moved incoming notes to `board/to_dev_rrule/read/`.
- Checked `board/STATUS.md`, `tracker/`, and `repo/` git status.

#### Fix for Issue #1218 / PR #1219 (Branch `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz`)
- **Bug**: In `_rrulestr._parse_date_value`, when parsing `EXDATE` or `DTSTART` with a `TZID` parameter, the code unconditionally attached the resolved `TZID` timezone to the parsed datetime object, even when `ignoretz=True`. This caused `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` in `.before()`, `.after()`, and `.between()`.
- **Implementation**: In `src/dateutil/rrule.py`, wrapped `TZID` lookup and timezone attachment in `if not ignoretz:`. When `ignoretz=True`, all parsed datetimes for `EXDATE` and `DTSTART` remain naive.
- **Unit Tests**: Added 4 unit test cases to `tests/test_rrule.py`:
- `testStrSetExDateWithTZIDIgnoreTZ`: verifies `EXDATE` lines with `TZID` yield naive datetimes when `ignoretz=True`.
- `testStrSetExDateValueDateTimeWithTZIDIgnoreTZ`: verifies `VALUE=DATE-TIME;TZID=...` with `ignoretz=True`.
- `testStrExDateTZIDIgnoreTZBefore`: directly tests reproduction from #1218 with `.before(now)` and `.before(now, inc=True)`.
- `testStrDtstartTZIDIgnoreTZ`: verifies `DTSTART;TZID=...` produces naive `_dtstart`.

- **Packaging**: Added Alec Rosenbaum to `AUTHORS.md` and added news fragment `changelog.d/1218.bugfix.rst`.
- **Git**: Committed to `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz` with author `dev_rrule <dev_rrule@dateutil.team>`.
- **Verification**: Ran `pytest tests/test_rrule.py` (565 passed, 1 xfailed) and full pytest suite (2036 passed, 47 skipped, 17 xfailed).
- **Tracker**: Replied to `tracker/issues/1218.md` and `tracker/pulls/1219.md`.

#### Investigation of Issue #1240 (DST Transition in `between()`)
- **Issue**: User observed `rules.between(target - timedelta(days=1), target + timedelta(minutes=1))` returning `[]` for an all-day event in `America/New_York` at `2022-11-07 04:53 UTC`.
- **Findings**:
- On Nov 6, 2022, `America/New_York` underwent autumn fall-back DST (EDT to EST), creating a **25-hour day**.
- Nov 6 midnight occurrence: 00:00 EDT = 04:00 UTC.
- Nov 7 midnight occurrence: 00:00 EST = 05:00 UTC.
- Physical elapsed time between occurrences is 25 hours.
- Query window `[04:53 UTC, 04:54 UTC]` has duration 24h 1m.

- Occurrence 1 (04:00 UTC) is before the window; Occurrence 2 (05:00 UTC) is after the window.
- `between()` returned `[]` completely correctly.
- **Resolution**: Provided full technical breakdown in `tracker/issues/1240.md` recommending calendar-aware boundaries rather than fixed 24-hour timedelta offsets.

#### Evaluation of PR #1123 (Dunder Methods on `rrule` and `rruleset`)
- **Analysis**:
- `rruleset` is an imperatively-constructed mutable builder. Adding `__hash__` violates Python's fundamental data model rule that mutable objects should not be hashable, risking silent hash table corruption.
- `rrule.__eq__` comparing `to_dict` constructor arguments defines syntactic rather than semantic equivalence, causing rules that generate the same recurrence set to be unequal.
- **Decision**: Recommended deferral past 2.9.0 (to 2.10 or 3.0) and replied on `tracker/pulls/1123.md`.

#### De-scoping PR #522 (RFC 7529 SKIP Option)
- Removed `release-blocker` tag on `tracker/pulls/522.md` and deferred to 2.10/3.0 due to incomplete RFC implementation.

#### Cross-Module Assistance: Issue #1242 / PR #1243 (`rrulebase` Pickling)
- Identified that pickling fails on `_tzicalvtz` and cached `rrulebase` due to `self._cache_lock` (`_thread.lock`) and `self._cache_gen` (generator).
- Shared clean `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` recipe with `dev_tz` (`board/to_dev_tz/6_dev_rrule_rrulebase_pickling_solution.md`) and on PR #1243 thread so cache does not need to be dropped.

#### Documentation Coordination: PR #844
- Coordinated with `docs` (`board/to_docs/6_dev_rrule_pr844_wkst_coordination.md`) endorsing PR #844 grammar improvements for `wkst`.
- Replied on `tracker/pulls/844.md`.

### 3. Board Communications Sent
- `board/to_rm/6_dev_rrule_rrule_status.md` (status of deliverables)
- `board/to_reviewer_a/6_dev_rrule_review_fix_1218.md` (review request for branch `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz`)
- `board/to_docs/6_dev_rrule_pr844_wkst_coordination.md` (PR #844 endorsement)
- `board/to_dev_tz/6_dev_rrule_rrulebase_pickling_solution.md` (rrulebase pickling solution)

### 4. What I Learned
- `_rrulestr._parse_date_value` had a subtle flaw where `TZID` assignment overrode `parser.parse(..., ignoretz=True)`.
- Autumn DST transitions create 25-hour calendar days where fixed 24h timedelta windows will miss midnight occurrences.
- Python mutable containers must avoid `__hash__`; `rrule` equality needs careful semantic specification.
- `_thread.lock` and generator objects require `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` to be excluded from pickle state.

### 5. What I Still Owe
- Await `reviewer_a` review of `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz` and merge into `main` upon approval.
- Assist `dev_tz` with `rrulebase` pickling changes if needed.
- Monitor `board/to_dev_rrule/` in next shift.

Fix test_tzlocal_offset_equal[GMT-tzoff1]

test_tzlocal_offset_equal[GMT-tzoff1] fails if a system does not
have a defined (installed) GMT timezone, for example if "Link Etc/GMT GMT"
is not defined in the zoneinfo configuration:

> assert tz.tzlocal() == tzoff
E AssertionError: assert tzlocal() == tzoffset(u'GMT', 0)
E -tzlocal()
E +tzoffset(u'GMT', 0)

An example of such a configuration is FreeBSD, who's default timezone is
UTC [1][2]. This configuration results in any "non-present" or undefined TZ
name being returned/processed as the default timezone name (in FreeBSD's
case, UTC).

Further, POSIX does not recognize [3] TZ=GMT or TZ=UTC as valid values
because they neither start with a colon nor contain a numeric offset hour
field.

Accordingly, update the GMT value for this parametrized test to GMT0, a
specific (not aliased) timezone, making it more robust to system
configuration differences.

[1] https://svnweb.freebsd.org/changeset/base/130332
[2] https://svnweb.freebsd.org/changeset/base/199405
[3] https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap08.html

### danieljnchen on 2023-04-03

I ran into the same issue myself -- the problem is that the `tzical` class doesn't support non-standard properties, as defined by [RFC 5545](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545#section-3.8.8.2). Google Calendar is one such vendor that likes to add these experimental properties into their timezone definitions (and their icalendar files in general); here is a simple example that reproduces this issue:

```
from dateutil.tz import tzical
from io import StringIO

# timezone definition from a Google Calendar ICS event
vtimezone = "BEGIN:VTIMEZONE
TZID:America/New_York
X-LIC-LOCATION:America/New_York
BEGIN:DAYLIGHT
DTSTART:19700308T020000
RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=2SU;BYMONTH=3
TZNAME:EDT
TZOFFSETFROM:-0500
TZOFFSETTO:-0400
END:DAYLIGHT
BEGIN:STANDARD
DTSTART:19701101T020000
RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=1SU;BYMONTH=11
TZNAME:EST
TZOFFSETFROM:-0400
TZOFFSETTO:-0500
END:STANDARD
END:VTIMEZONE"

with StringIO(vtimezone) as tz_file:
tz = tzical(tz_file) # ValueError
```

[RFC 5545](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545#section-3.2) specifies that
> Applications MUST ignore x-param and iana-param values they don't recognize.

and additionally includes `x-prop` as a valid property of a VTIMEZONE component ([source](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545#section-3.6.5)), so I believe that this is a bug that dateutil should handle. It should be pretty simple to fix this; I'll make a PR.

In the meantime, you can get your code working by parsing out the non-standard properties before passing your file to `tzical`:
```
import re
from dateutil.tz import tzical
from io import StringIO

timezone_file = "your_timezone_file.ics"
with open(timezone_file, "r") as f:
vtimezone = f.read()

# NOTE: this doesn't handle line folding
# If you want to handle experimental attributes that are on lines that may
# be folded, refer to this code:
# https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/master/src/dateutil/tz/tz.py#L1335
clean_vtimezone = re.sub("X-.+?(\r\n|\n)", "", vtimezone)
with StringIO(clean_vtimezone) as tz_file:
tz = tzical(tz_file)
```

```bash
$ python -c "import dateutil; print(dateutil.__version__)"
2.8.2
$ python --version
Python 3.8.10
```

I realize that 2.8.0 was released in 2019, but this change makes upgrading a bit difficult as the new EXDATE parameter parsing makes the behavior not backwards compatible. The workaround seems to be passing both a tz-aware datetime to `dtstart` and `.before(dt)` if there's a `TZID` included on `EXDATE`. Though it's sort of hard to tell beforehand if there's going to be a `TZID` parameter there.
I would expect that passing `ignoretz=True` to`rrulestr` would make `EXDATE` parsing ignore any `TZID`.
Fixed in branch `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz` (PR #1219).

In `_rrulestr._parse_date_value`, the `TZID` parameter is now only resolved and applied to parsed datetime objects when `ignoretz=False`. When `ignoretz=True`, all parsed datetimes for `EXDATE` (and `DTSTART`) remain timezone-naive, resolving the `TypeError` during comparisons in methods like `.before()`, `.after()`, and `.between()`. Comprehensive unit tests covering both `EXDATE` and `DTSTART` with `TZID` and `ignoretz=True` have been added to `tests/test_rrule.py`.
Reviewed and approved branch `fix-1218-exdate-ignoretz`.

- Confirmed fix in `src/dateutil/rrule.py`: guarding `TZID` parameter processing and assignment behind `if not ignoretz:` ensures datetimes remain timezone-naive when `ignoretz=True`.
- Verified that comparison methods (`.before()`, `.after()`, `.between()`) operate without raising `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`.
- Verified 4 new regression tests in `tests/test_rrule.py` passing, along with the full rrule test suite (565 passed).
- Verified `AUTHORS.md` entry for Alec Rosenbaum and news fragment in `changelog.d/1218.bugfix.rst`. Approved for merge to `main`.

# #1239 Use SPDX license expression in project metadata
pull request, state: open, labels: none, opened by RazerM on 2022-11-03

<!-- First time contributors: Take a moment to review CONTRIBUTING.md! -->
<!-- Remove sections if not applicable -->
## Summary of changes

As a downstream user it is desirable to be able to programmatically determine the precise licenses used by our dependencies. The emerging convention for this is the [SPDX License List](https://spdx.org/licenses/). SPDX License Expressions are already used in the JavaScript (npm) and Rust (crates.io) ecosystems, for example.
In Python, there is [PEP 639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/) which would add a standard 'License-Expression' metadata field. The discussion around this PEP seems to have gone stale in 2021.

This merge request is in lieu of that PEP coming soon. Unless you as project maintainers think the proposed change in this PR has downsides (which you are entitled to!), I would ask that you accept this change so that it's possible for users to attempt to parse your license metadata as an SPDX License Expression.

It's my understanding that old contributions are not available under the Apache-2.0 license and therefore the license expression must be `Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause` rather than `Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause`.

# Relativedelta, Easter & Utils Triage for 2.9.0
Here is the triage breakdown for `dateutil/relativedelta`, `dateutil/easter`, and `dateutil/utils`:

## 1. Critical Bug: Issue #1157 & PR #1158 (MUST MERGE)
- **Problem**:
In `relativedelta.py`:
```python
def __ne__(self, other):
return not self.__eq__(other)
```
When comparing `relativedelta` with an incompatible type (such as `None` or an int), `self.__eq__(other)` returns `NotImplemented`.

- In Python < 3.12: `bool(NotImplemented)` is `True`, so `not NotImplemented` evaluates to `False`. Thus `relativedelta() != None` returns `False`!
- In Python 3.12+ and 3.14: Using `NotImplemented` in a boolean context raises:
`TypeError: NotImplemented should not be used in a boolean context`.
- **Solution in PR #1158**:
Simply removes the custom `__ne__` method entirely. In Python, removing `__ne__` allows the default object model to invert `__eq__` properly and handle `NotImplemented` fallback.
PR #1158 has unit tests, AUTHORS update, and changelog entry. Ready to merge!

## 2. Other PRs for Review
- **PR #1115 (fixes Issue #1114)**:
- Fixes inconsistent behavior in division and multiplication of `relativedelta`. Includes tests, AUTHORS entry, and news fragment.
- **PR #924 (fixes Issue #920)**:
- Adds support for float months in `relativedelta`.
- **PR #1210**:
- Adds helper method for constructing `relativedelta` from an ISO 8601 duration string.
- **PR #768**:
- Adds function type annotations to `dateutil/utils.py`.

# Critical Blocker: relativedelta.__ne__ TypeError on Python 3.12+ / 3.14

**To**: dev_core
**From**: rm
**Date**: Shift 10
**Subject**: URGENT - PR #1158 / Issue #1157 runtime crash on modern Python
During test verification in Shift 10 on our Python 3.14 environment, we encountered an immediate runtime failure with `relativedelta`:

```python
>>> from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta
>>> rd = relativedelta(days=1)
>>> rd != None
Traceback (most recent call last):
File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
File "src/dateutil/relativedelta.py", line 568, in __ne__
return not self.__eq__(other)

TypeError: NotImplemented should not be used in a boolean context
```

### Technical Root Cause:
In `src/dateutil/relativedelta.py`:
```python
def __ne__(self, other):
return not self.__eq__(other)
```
When `self.__eq__(other)` is called with an incompatible type like `None`, it returns `NotImplemented`. In Python 3.12+ (and enforced in 3.14), calling `not NotImplemented` raises `TypeError: NotImplemented should not be used in a boolean context`. (In earlier Python versions, this silently returned `False` for `rd != None`!).

### Required Action:
This elevates **PR #1158 (Issue #1157)** to a **Critical Release Blocker**:
1. Remove `def __ne__(self, other):` entirely from `src/dateutil/relativedelta.py`. Python's data model automatically falls back to inverting `__eq__` properly and handles `NotImplemented` delegations without evaluating it in a boolean context.
2. Add regression tests in `tests/test_relativedelta.py` verifying `rd != None`, `rd != 15`, `rd != "string"`, and `rd == None`.
3. Add `kevinkt1` to `AUTHORS.md`.
4. Add news fragment `changelog.d/1158.bugfix.rst`.
5. Branch as `fix-1158-relativedelta-ne` and submit for code review to `board/to_reviewer_b/` (or `board/to_reviewer_a/`).
Please make this your top priority for your next shift.

# #1266 Set github workflow permissions as read only
issue, state: open, labels: none, opened by joycebrum on 2023-02-27
Hi, I'm Joyce from Google and I'm working with the OpenSSF to improve supply-chain security in many open source projects.

The first supply-chain improvement I would like to suggest is to restrict the permissions given by the github to GITHUB_TOKEN on the workflow run. This is important because github, by default, grants all write permissions to GITHUB_TOKEN (similar to `permissions: write-all`), which could be exploit by an attacker in case of a compromised workflow.

Thus, it is both a recommendation from [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions) and the [Github](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions) to always use credentials that are minimally scoped.

I would like to suggest a PR setting the top level permission of each workflow to `contents: read` (usually the actions only need this) and grand any other read or write permission needed in the job level.
Let me know if the PR is welcome and I'll suggest it ASAP.

### What I Learned
- In `dateutil.tz`, `tzutc` and `tzoffset` are designed to be singletons, but `object.__reduce__` bypasses `__new__` when unpickling unless `__reduce__` returns `(cls, args)`. Returning the constructor tuple ensures unpickling goes through the caching logic.
- RFC 5545 explicitly accommodates `X-` extension properties. While `tzical` enforces strict property parsing, ignoring `X-` prefixed properties allows broad compatibility with calendar exports from vendors like Google Calendar.
- The bundled zoneinfo file `dateutil-zoneinfo.tar.gz` was missing in `main` due to an earlier commit moving to src-layout. Branch `update-1283-bundled-zoneinfo` restores it, updating timezone definitions to IANA `2026d` and fixing DST abolition for Mexico City.

### danieljnchen on 2023-04-03

I ran into the same issue myself -- the problem is that the `tzical` class doesn't support non-standard properties, as defined by [RFC 5545](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545#section-3.8.8.2). Google Calendar is one such vendor that likes to add these experimental properties into their timezone definitions (and their icalendar files in general); here is a simple example that reproduces this issue:

```
from dateutil.tz import tzical
from io import StringIO

# timezone definition from a Google Calendar ICS event
vtimezone = "BEGIN:VTIMEZONE
TZID:America/New_York
X-LIC-LOCATION:America/New_York
BEGIN:DAYLIGHT
DTSTART:19700308T020000
RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=2SU;BYMONTH=3
TZNAME:EDT
TZOFFSETFROM:-0500
TZOFFSETTO:-0400
END:DAYLIGHT
BEGIN:STANDARD
DTSTART:19701101T020000
RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=1SU;BYMONTH=11
TZNAME:EST
TZOFFSETFROM:-0400
TZOFFSETTO:-0500
END:STANDARD
END:VTIMEZONE"

with StringIO(vtimezone) as tz_file:
tz = tzical(tz_file) # ValueError
```

[RFC 5545](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545#section-3.2) specifies that
> Applications MUST ignore x-param and iana-param values they don't recognize.

and additionally includes `x-prop` as a valid property of a VTIMEZONE component ([source](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545#section-3.6.5)), so I believe that this is a bug that dateutil should handle. It should be pretty simple to fix this; I'll make a PR.

In the meantime, you can get your code working by parsing out the non-standard properties before passing your file to `tzical`:
```
import re
from dateutil.tz import tzical
from io import StringIO

timezone_file = "your_timezone_file.ics"
with open(timezone_file, "r") as f:
vtimezone = f.read()

# NOTE: this doesn't handle line folding
# If you want to handle experimental attributes that are on lines that may
# be folded, refer to this code:
# https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/master/src/dateutil/tz/tz.py#L1335
clean_vtimezone = re.sub("X-.+?(\r\n|\n)", "", vtimezone)
with StringIO(clean_vtimezone) as tz_file:
tz = tzical(tz_file)
```

# #1239 Use SPDX license expression in project metadata
pull request, state: open, labels: none, opened by RazerM on 2022-11-03

<!-- First time contributors: Take a moment to review CONTRIBUTING.md! -->
<!-- Remove sections if not applicable -->
## Summary of changes

As a downstream user it is desirable to be able to programmatically determine the precise licenses used by our dependencies. The emerging convention for this is the [SPDX License List](https://spdx.org/licenses/). SPDX License Expressions are already used in the JavaScript (npm) and Rust (crates.io) ecosystems, for example.
In Python, there is [PEP 639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/) which would add a standard 'License-Expression' metadata field. The discussion around this PEP seems to have gone stale in 2021.

This merge request is in lieu of that PEP coming soon. Unless you as project maintainers think the proposed change in this PR has downsides (which you are entitled to!), I would ask that you accept this change so that it's possible for users to attempt to parse your license metadata as an SPDX License Expression.

It's my understanding that old contributions are not available under the Apache-2.0 license and therefore the license expression must be `Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause` rather than `Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause`.

issue, state: open, labels: none, opened by joycebrum on 2023-02-27
Hi, I'm Joyce from Google and I'm working with the OpenSSF to improve supply-chain security in many open source projects.

The first supply-chain improvement I would like to suggest is to restrict the permissions given by the github to GITHUB_TOKEN on the workflow run. This is important because github, by default, grants all write permissions to GITHUB_TOKEN (similar to `permissions: write-all`), which could be exploit by an attacker in case of a compromised workflow.

Thus, it is both a recommendation from [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions) and the [Github](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions) to always use credentials that are minimally scoped.

I would like to suggest a PR setting the top level permission of each workflow to `contents: read` (usually the actions only need this) and grand any other read or write permission needed in the job level.
Let me know if the PR is welcome and I'll suggest it ASAP.

The code checks for hour, minute, and second components by extracting two characters each, using `timestr[pos:pos + 2]`. A critical condition arises if the remaining string length is less than two, which would trigger a `ValueError`. Considering `timestr = "12:1"`, the hour extraction will work but minute extraction would fail. This scenario demonstrates an edge case in the input string handling.

Examining several time string variations, including those with missing components or incorrect lengths, consistently reveals the `ValueError` arising when the remaining string length is less than two after parsing hours and minutes or hours and minutes. The code correctly parses valid time strings like "1234", "12", but fails with "121" or "12345" due to the insufficient remaining string length check. Analyzing `20200728121240` reveals a date parsing issue where the function incorrectly separates date and time, leading to `time_str` containing an invalid substring.

Considering the specific case of parsing "21240", the original logic would incorrectly extract "0" as the minute's second digit, leading to an incorrect result. The introduced check, `if len_str - pos < 2`, correctly prevents this. Further investigation confirmed that hour, minute, and second components always require two digits in ISO 8601 format, validating the error's correctness. Timezone parsing is handled separately, confirming the edge case is accurately addressed.

The analysis expanded to include related parsing functions. `_parse_isodate_common` already included the necessary length checks, unlike the initial target `_parse_isotime`. Examining `_parse_isodate_uncommon` revealed a similar slicing vulnerability when parsing the week number. The identified condition `if len(dt_str) - pos < 2` was added to validate week numbers, ensuring code consistency.

# #1318 Multiplying relativedelta with fractional days ends up with truncated values
issue, state: open, labels: none, opened by jrmylow on 2023-11-12
Multiplying a `relativedelta` with non-integer day values (e.g. `relativedelta(days=+1.5)` converts to integer values of days, losing information in the process.

The cause appears to be applying a blanket `int()` to the results of the multiplication [L495](https://github.com/dateutil/dateutil/blob/296d419fe6bf3b22897f8f210735ac9c4e1cb796/src/dateutil/relativedelta.py#L495), without checking to see if fractional days should be converted down into hours/seconds etc.

Is this intended behaviour? Currently `relativedelta` accepts non-integer values for days (as does the python standard library), so my current assumption is that it should mirror the behaviour from `datetime` and convert fractional days.

Minimal reproducible example:
```python
import dateutil
delta = dateutil.relativedelta.relativedelta(days=1.5)
print(delta) # relativedelta(days=+1.5)
print(delta * 1) # relativedelta(days=+1)
```

By contrast, `datetime.timedelta` from the standard library does not lose the half-day:
```python
import datetime
delta = datetime.timedelta(days=1.5)
print(delta) # datetime.timedelta(days=1, seconds=43200)
print(delta * 1) # datetime.timedelta(days=1, seconds=43200)
```

Dateutil version: `2.8.2`
Python version: `3.10.4`

# #1325 python-dateutil returns "naive" datetime objects
issue, state: open, labels: none, opened by mlasch on 2023-11-28
The Python `datetime` module from the standard lib supports so called "naive" and "time zone aware" `datetime` objects: https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#aware-and-naive-objects

As far as I can see, `dateutil` returns in some (all?) cases naive datetime objects. Using naive objects is discouraged (is it?) and deprecated since version 3.12 (https://blog.miguelgrinberg.com/post/it-s-time-for-a-change-datetime-utcnow-is-now-deprecated).
Let's say, I want to compare the result from `tzstr.transitions()` I get a TypeError (Tested with Python3.10):

```Python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import dateutil.tz

now = datetime.now(timezone.utc) # recommended to replace utcnow()
posix_zone = dateutil.tz.tzstr("CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3")
start, end = posix_zone.transitions(2023)
now > start
```
Also the output of `start.timestamp()` will depend on the timezone the code is running.

```
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[27], line 7
5 posix_zone = dateutil.tz.tzstr("CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3")
6 start, end = posix_zone.transitions(2023)
----> 7 now > start

TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
```
This makes sense, as I don't want to compare UTC times with a unspecified time. A workaround for me is to set UTC manually for the returned objects. I have to assume that the native `datetime` object represents UTC.
```
start = start.astimezone(timezone.utc)
end = end.astimezone(timezone.utc)
```
Should `dateutil` return time zone aware `datetime` objects, now that it looks like the naive type will be phased out sooner or later?

Suppose you want to know how much time is left, in
years/months/days/etc, before the next easter happening on a
year with a Friday 13th in August, and you want to get today's
date out of the "date" unix system command. Here is the code:

>>> from dateutil.relativedelta import *
>>> from dateutil.easter import *
>>> from dateutil.rrule import *
>>> from dateutil.parser import *
>>> from datetime import *
>>> now = parse("Sat Oct 11 17:13:46 UTC 2003")
>>> today = now.date()
>>> year = rrule(YEARLY,dtstart=now,bymonth=8,bymonthday=13,byweekday=FR)[0].year

>>> rdelta = relativedelta(easter(year), today)
>>> print("Today is: %s" % today)
Today is: 2003-10-11
>>> print("Year with next Aug 13th on a Friday is: %s" % year)
Year with next Aug 13th on a Friday is: 2004
>>> print("How far is the Easter of that year: %s" % rdelta)
How far is the Easter of that year: relativedelta(months=+6)
>>> print("And the Easter of that year is: %s" % (today+rdelta))
And the Easter of that year is: 2004-04-11
Being exactly 6 months ahead was **really** a coincidence :)

Hi, I'm Joyce from Google and I'm working with the OpenSSF to improve supply-chain security in many open source projects.

The first supply-chain improvement I would like to suggest is to restrict the permissions given by the github to GITHUB_TOKEN on the workflow run. This is important because github, by default, grants all write permissions to GITHUB_TOKEN (similar to `permissions: write-all`), which could be exploit by an attacker in case of a compromised workflow.

Thus, it is both a recommendation from [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions) and the [Github](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions) to always use credentials that are minimally scoped.

I would like to suggest a PR setting the top level permission of each workflow to `contents: read` (usually the actions only need this) and grand any other read or write permission needed in the job level.
Let me know if the PR is welcome and I'll suggest it ASAP.

Added note into docs and tests where relativedelta would return last day of the month
only if the same day on a different month resolves to a date that doesn't exist.
Reported by @hawkEye-01 (gh issue #1167). Fixed by @Mifrill (gh pr #1168)

==> changelog.d/1007.feature.rst <==
Made all ``dateutil`` submodules lazily imported using `PEP 562
<https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0562/>`_. On Python 3.7+, things like
``import dateutil; dateutil.tz.gettz("America/New_York")`` will now work
without explicitly importing ``dateutil.tz``, with the import occurring behind
the scenes on first use. The old behavior remains on Python 3.6 and earlier.
Fixed by Orson Adams. (gh issue #771, gh pr #1007)

==> changelog.d/1044.bugfix.rst <==
Do not require ``setuptools.command.test`` in ``setup.py``, which was deprecated and removed in recent setuptools versions. Reported and resolved by Diego Barrios Romero (gh pr #1044).

==> changelog.d/1053.bugfix.rst <==
Fixed a bug where unpickling a datetime with ``tzutc`` or ``tzoffset`` created
a new, different instance rather than restoring the singleton instance.
Reported and fixed by masipcat. (gh issue #1051, gh pr #1053)

==> changelog.d/1167.doc.rst <==
Added note into docs and tests where relativedelta would return last day of the month
only if the same day on a different month resolves to a date that doesn't exist.
Reported by @hawkEye-01 (gh issue #1167). Fixed by @Mifrill (gh pr #1168)
==> changelog.d/1174.misc.rst <==
Added Python 3.10 to the test matrix and Trove classifiers. Fixed by @hugovk (gh pr #1174)

==> changelog.d/1211.misc.rst <==
Test with Python 3.11-dev. Reported and fixed by Hugo van Kemenade (gh pr #1211).

==> changelog.d/1218.bugfix.rst <==
Fixed a bug where ``ignoretz=True`` was not respected when parsing ``EXDATE``
and ``DTSTART`` properties with ``TZID`` parameters in ``rrulestr``.
Reported by Alec Rosenbaum. (gh pr #1219, issue #1218)

==> changelog.d/1233.misc.rst <==
Added support and PyPI classifiers for Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 (gh issue #1233).

==> changelog.d/1236.bugfix.rst <==
Fixed a bug in ``isoparser`` where week 53 was accepted for years that have only
52 ISO weeks. Reported and fixed by Ev2geny and dev_parser. (gh issue #1236)

==> changelog.d/1239.misc.rst <==
Use SPDX license expression in project metadata. Contributed by Frazer McLean (gh pr #1239).

==> changelog.d/1261.bugfix.rst <==
Convert ``passenv`` in ``tox.ini`` to multiline list to support tox 4. Reported and resolved by Marcel Telka (gh issue #1261).

==> changelog.d/1273.bugfix.rst <==
Ignored non-standard properties starting with ``X-`` when parsing icalendar
timezones in ``tzical`` per RFC 5545. Reported and fixed by Daniel Chen.
(gh issue #1185, gh pr #1273)

==> changelog.d/1283.data.rst <==
Updated bundled tzdata version to 2026d. (gh issue #1283)

==> changelog.d/1284.bugfix.rst <==
Fixed ``DeprecationWarning`` on Python 3.12+ caused by deprecated
``datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(0)`` in ``dateutil.tz``.
Reported by Hugo van Kemenade. (gh issue #1284)

==> changelog.d/1300.misc.rst <==
Added Python 3.12 to GitHub Actions test matrix and added main to branch triggers. Reported by @stegayet (gh pr #1300).

without explicitly importing ``dateutil.tz``, with the import occurring behind
the scenes on first use. The old behavior remains on Python 3.6 and earlier.

a new, different instance rather than restoring the singleton instance.

allocation of ``__dict__`` in subclasses defining ``__slots__``.

Parsing a local tzname
----------------------

Three-character time zone abbreviations are *not* unique in that they do not explicitly map to a time zone. A list of time zone abbreviations in use can be found `here <https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zones/>`_. This means that parsing a datetime string such as ``'2018-01-01 12:30:30 CST'`` is ambiguous without context. Using :mod:`dateutil.parser` and :mod:`dateutil.tz`, it is possible to provide a context such that these local names are converted to proper time zones.

``import dateutil; dateutil.tz.gettz("America/New_York")`` will now work
without explicitly importing ``dateutil.tz``, with the import occurring behind
the scenes on first use. The old behavior remains on Python 3.6 and earlier.
Fixed by Orson Adams. (gh issue #771, gh pr #1007)

- Do not require ``setuptools.command.test`` in ``setup.py``, which was deprecated and removed in recent setuptools versions. Reported and resolved by Diego Barrios Romero (gh pr #1044).
- Fixed a bug where unpickling a datetime with ``tzutc`` or ``tzoffset`` created
a new, different instance rather than restoring the singleton instance.
Reported and fixed by masipcat. (gh issue #1051, gh pr #1053)
- Fixed a bug where ``ignoretz=True`` was not respected when parsing ``EXDATE``
and ``DTSTART`` properties with ``TZID`` parameters in ``rrulestr``.
Reported by Alec Rosenbaum. (gh pr #1219, issue #1218)
- Fixed a bug in ``isoparser`` where week 53 was accepted for years that have only

52 ISO weeks. Reported and fixed by Ev2geny and dev_parser. (gh issue #1236)
- Convert ``passenv`` in ``tox.ini`` to multiline list to support tox 4. Reported and resolved by Marcel Telka (gh issue #1261).
- Ignored non-standard properties starting with ``X-`` when parsing icalendar
timezones in ``tzical`` per RFC 5545. Reported and fixed by Daniel Chen.
(gh issue #1185, gh pr #1273)
- Fixed ``DeprecationWarning`` on Python 3.12+ caused by deprecated
``datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(0)`` in ``dateutil.tz``.
Reported by Hugo van Kemenade. (gh issue #1284)

Documentation changes
---------------------

- Clarified ``wkst`` parameter documentation and docstrings in ``rrule``. Contributed by @SavenR (gh pr #844).
- Added solution to "Next Monday meeting" documentation exercise. Contributed by @ffe4 (gh issue #665, gh pr #1016).
- Fixed country name typo in documentation exercises. Contributed by @diceroll123 (gh pr #1037).
- Cleaned up quick example code in ``README.rst`` to use explicit imports. Contributed by @eumiro (gh pr #1095).
- Added note into docs and tests where relativedelta would return last day of the month
only if the same day on a different month resolves to a date that doesn't exist.
Reported by @hawkEye-01 (gh issue #1167). Fixed by @Mifrill (gh pr #1168)
- Added caution note to ``parser.parse`` documentation clarifying that parsing non-datetime strings produces undefined behavior. Reported by Paul Ganssle (gh issue #1270). Contributed by @madt2709 (gh pr #1281).

- Added example of ``isoparse`` usage to documentation. Reported by Denis Prisbrey (gh issue #1073). Contributed by @rbarman (gh pr #1322).
- Updated ``README.rst`` to reference the IANA Time Zone Database. Contributed by @clach04 (gh pr #1326).

- Added Python 3.10 to the test matrix and Trove classifiers. Fixed by @hugovk (gh pr #1174)
- Test with Python 3.11-dev. Reported and fixed by Hugo van Kemenade (gh pr #1211).
- Added support and PyPI classifiers for Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 (gh issue #1233).
- Use SPDX license expression in project metadata. Contributed by Frazer McLean (gh pr #1239).
- Added Python 3.12 to GitHub Actions test matrix and added main to branch triggers. Reported by @stegayet (gh pr #1300).
- Explicitly set permissions to contents: read in GitHub Actions workflows. Contributed by @joycebrum (gh pr #1303).
- Updated Read the Docs configuration to specify build OS and modern Python version. Contributed by Paul Ganssle (gh pr #1319).

# #1186 Missing `__slots__` in `parser._parser._resultbase`
issue, state: open, labels: none, opened by ariebovenberg on 2022-01-21

Both `_tzparser._result` and `parser._result` have slots and inherit from `_resultbase`, which does not have slots. This reduces the memory savings from `__slots__`, and doesn't prevent `__dict__` from being created.
solution: add `__slots__` to `parser._parser._resultbase`

- **Problem**: `_resultbase` lacked `__slots__ = ()`, causing subclasses (`parser._result`, `_tzparser._result`, `_attr`) to instantiate unnecessary `__dict__`.

a new, different instance rather than restoring the singleton instance.

and ``DTSTART`` properties with ``TZID`` parameters in ``rrulestr``.

52 ISO weeks. Reported and fixed by Ev2geny and dev_parser. (gh issue #1236)

timezones in ``tzical`` per RFC 5545. Reported and fixed by Daniel Chen.

``datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(0)`` in ``dateutil.tz``.
